authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 14024 hasta gives Middle Indo-Aryan hattha, Hindi hāth, Marathi/Nepali hāt and eastern hāt/hāta, with both hand and forearm senses; Torwali hatth and Palula hāt support the included Dardic hand/arm forms.

assignments.Notes: CDIAL 14024 hasta gives Middle Indo-Aryan hattha, Hindi hāth, Marathi/Nepali hāt and eastern hāt/hāta, with both hand and forearm senses; Torwali hatth and Palula hāt support the included Dardic hand/arm forms. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 5889.1 explicitly lists nominative Kalasha tu, Khowar tu and Gawri tu, as well as Hindi tū, Punjabi tū̃, Marathi tū̃ and other regional singular pronouns. The addendum confirms Khowar nominative tu versus oblique ta. Honorific/formal labels do not change the nominative family; analogical remodeling is acknowledged in the article.
